summary: Bethlehem summit fire lookout site; tower gone, summit now private with an observatory on the old site; county sources conflict.

facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone. The summit now has an observatory built around the old tower site and communication towers.

access.note: The summit is privately owned. NH Family Hikes says the owner welcomes hikers, but the route follows a private road.

visit.trail_note: Route follows a private road to the summit, which NH Family Hikes says is hard to find

corrections.why: Wikipedia places Mount Agassiz in the town of Bethlehem, Grafton County. FFLA and the Eastern US Lookouts page both say Coos. Editor should confirm before changing the record.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA and the Eastern US Lookouts page list Coos County. Wikipedia places Bethlehem, and so the mountain, in Grafton County. The story names the town and says the sources disagree.

notes_for_editor: No build date or removal date for the Agassiz tower was found, so none is given. County conflicts (Coos vs Grafton). The communication-tower description rests on one hiking blog; no owner or agency statement found. Did not visit; the summit is private land. Brief's agency field is blank and was left out.
